sentences.text: G.S. SANDHAWALIA.J (Oral)
1. The present judgement shall dispose of the above mentioned two writ petitions as common issue is involved therein.

2. Challenge in the present writ petitions is to the notification dated 17.11.2005 (Annexure P-1)
issued under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short the 1894 Act), the subsequent notification dated 07.02.2006 (Annexure P-2) issued under Section 6 of the 1894 Act 1 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:144041-DB CWP-7530-2016 & connected petition -2- and consequently the award dated 02.03.2006 (Annexure P-3) qua the land situated in the revenue estate of villages Badh Khalsa, Jakhuli, Bahalgarh, Tehsil & District Sonipat, on the ground of proceedings have been lapsed.

Challenge has also been raised to the speaking order dated 02.03.2016 (Annexure P-15),
whereby the authorities have rejected the case for the said relief of release of land, on the claim that the land in question is lying vacant at the site and 80% of the compensation has been disbursed of the amount deposited.
3.

In CWP-7530-2016, land of the petitioners falling in village Badh Khalsa affects plot no.40 and development has been completed in the entire land of the sector except the land of the petitioners and other stay matters for setting up of Rajiv Gandhi Education City.
The recommendation of the Zonal Committee was not to release the land.

It is pertinent to notice that on an earlier occasion the matter had been decided on 30.10.2017 on the issue that compensation had not been paid and thus,
the proceedings have been lapsed.

The said order has been set aside by the Apex Court in a bunch of cases titled as State of Haryana and others Vs. Anil Kumar and others SLP (C) No.1554-2019 and the matter was remanded to decide issues other than one covered by case of Indore Development Authority Vs. Manohar Lal and others (2020) 8 SCC 129.
4.

sentences.text:
Similarly, in CWP-24888-2016 there is a speaking order dated 08.07.2016 (Annexure P-8)
pertaining to land in village Asarwepur, wherein also there is a rejection on the ground that the site affects the commercial area, 30 meter road and 2 no. hostel sites.
The site was vacant before Section 4 notification but house and shops are constructed at present.

The development works have been completed and the claimed land affects 2 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:144041-DB CWP-7530-2016 & connected petition -3- 30 meters wide road and other services and no allotment could be made on site of the petitioner and no third party rights could have been created on the land of the petitioners and therefore, the case for release of land was rejected.

4. In the first petition i.e. CWP-7530-2016, it is the own case of the petitioner that after the award was passed on 02.03.2006, CWP-3832- 2006 was dismissed on 31.05.2006 by a Division Bench of this Court and the said order was further upheld by the Apex Court in SLP (C) No.15269- 2006 on 22.09.2006.
The second round of litigation was initiated by filing CWP-23996-2013, which was also dismissed as withdrawn after arguing the same for some time on 11.11.2013.
The third round was then initiated by filing CWP-18047-2014, whereby the directions were given to pass a speaking order, which is now subject matter of challenge.

A perusal of the earlier order would go on to reveal that the Coordinate Bench of this Court noticed the earlier history and only on account of the fact that petitioner was still in physical possession and no compensation was paid to him, the matter, at Virender Kumar vs State Of Haryana And Others on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106401866/
2 that point of time, was directed to be considered since position of law was not clear at that point of time.

sentences.text: It was under such circumstances that the lis has been kept alive, though, it had long died when the award was passed on 02.03.2006 and the land had vested in the State and the subsequent litigation has been finalized up to the Apex Court in the form of SLP(C)-15269 of 2006 decided on 22.09.2006.
The remand is also specific on the ground that if any other issue survives, the matter is to be taken up.

5. The speaking order would go on to show that the land measuring 15 kanal 12 marla had been handed over vide Rapat No.566 dated 02.03.2006 and it was vacant at the site and 80% of the compensation 3 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:144041-DB CWP-7530-2016 & connected petition -4- had been disbursed.

When the earlier matter was dismissed on 31.05.2006 in terms of CWP-4300-2006 titled as Jai Parkash Vs. State of Haryana and others, wherein acquisition for setting up Rajiv Gandhi Education City, had been upheld.

entities.text: Jai Parkash Vs. State of Haryana and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On 11.11.2013 when the second writ petition was dismissed as withdrawn after arguing for some time and with liberty to the petitioners to pursue the case with the administrative authorities.
Thus, litigation has been finalized and was only revived by virtue of order, whereby the representation was to be decided and it would not give a fresh cause of action.
Thus, we do not find any plausible reason, which would require consideration in view of the limited extent the matter has been examined by this Court, in view of the remand order.

6. In CWP-7530-2016, it is also mentioned in the reply that no objections were filed under Section 5 A of the 1894 Act when the acquisition was done and out of the award amount of Rs.3,34,90,10,540/- deposited, Rs.2,60,58,18,572/- has already been disbursed among the land owners and rest of the amount is lying deposited before L.A.C.
6.

In CWP-24888-2016 the land measures 22 kanal 14 marla situated in the revenue estate of village Aswarpur, Tehsil Rai, District Sonipat, which is part of the same acquisition, whereby 9 villages were subject matter of acquisition and the total land acquired was 2006.50 acres for the purpose of setting up Education City.

The reply filed would go on to show that the land was vacant at the time of issuing notification under Section 4 of the 1894 Act vide Rapat Roznamcha No.71 dated 02.03.2006 had also been entered and the land was handed over to the beneficiary department and thus vested in the State at that point of time.

The acquisition having been accepted, though, the writ petition had earlier been 4 of 6 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:144041-DB CWP-7530-2016 &
connected petition -5- decided on 30.10.2017 but is also subject matter of remand in a bunch of cases in Anil Kumar's case (supra).
7.

In view of the limited extent, the prayer is only on account of the lapsing and therefore nothing on merits is to be decided to that extent except the consideration of speaking order dated 21.07.2016 passed in view of the earlier directions got issued from this Court.
A perusal of the impugned order would go on to show that the land is required for planned development.
The lay out plan is also appended with the petition as Annexure R-2.
The land in question falls in the planned development of the area and one portion is extending into the 30 meter wide road also apart from the affecting the size of Plot No.6B 1A hostel.

The land stood apparently vested in the year 2006 and there was no challenge to the said vesting and only on account of the controversy of lapsing, the writ petition has Virender Kumar vs State Of Haryana And Others on 5 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106401866/
3 been filed in the year 2014 for the first time, whereby the prayer was made for deciding the representation, which has been duly rejected.
8.

sentences.text: In such circumstances, having accepted the acquisition proceedings, nothing survives.

However,
keeping in view the findings have been recorded that the construction has been raised in the present case after passing of the award, we are of the considered view that the petitioners in CWP-24888-2016 would be given six months time to vacate the structures which they have allegedly raised without any right as the land stood vested in the State.
8. Accordingly, keeping in view the above discussion, both the writ petitions are dismissed.
5 of 6  Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:144041-DB CWP-7530-2016 & connected petition -6- 9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand disposed of.
(G.S. SANDHAWALIA)
